otoc-echo-v1.name: Quantum Echo
otoc-echo-v1.description: Perturb a scrambled qubit chain, reverse it, and listen for what returns — a signed, complex multi-tap delay map.

allow_high_shots.description: Permit shots above 8192 (QPU time scales linearly).
allow_high_shots.title: Allow High Shots

depth.description: Echo depths t = 1..depth — the tap time slots. Each circuit has 2·depth layers.
depth.title: Depth

disorder.description: Additive per-gate angle jitter, std in radians. 0 = clean Floquet. Localises the echo; the only lever that makes `seed` matter.
disorder.title: Disorder

exact.description: aer only: exact (infinite-shot) expectation values instead of sampling.
exact.title: Exact

fractional_gates.description: Use native rzz/rx on hardware where available. Halves the forward half's two-qubit count; disables gate twirling.
fractional_gates.title: Fractional Gates

include_taps.description: Also emit a flattened tap list (site, depth, F_re, F_im, level, polarity) in extras.
include_taps.title: Include Taps

include_z.description: Also measure <Z_i>, completing each site's Bloch vector. Free on aer; a third measurement basis (1.5x shots) on hardware.
include_z.title: Include Z

kick.description: Perturbation Pauli applied to the kick site between U and U†.
kick.title: Kick

kick_site.description: Regeneration source: the site that receives the impulse. Default: centre.
kick_site.title: Kick Site

lattice.description: Topology of the delay line. `chain`: site → pan. `square` (Nighthawk-native): x → pan, y → diffusion.
lattice.title: Lattice

machine.description: Backend: 'aer' (local, noiseless) or an IBM backend name such as 'ibm_phoenix'.
machine.title: Machine

min_tap_level.description: |F| threshold for the emitted tap list.
min_tap_level.title: Min Tap Level

n_sites.description: Chain length in qubits (= pan positions). Ignored for `square`.
n_sites.title: N Sites

qpu_instance.description: IBM Quantum instance CRN. As with the token: required for `via: direct`, optional BYOK for `via: mothbackend`.
qpu_instance.title: Qpu Instance

qpu_token.description: IBM Quantum API token. Required for `via: direct` on an IBM machine (or the QISKIT_IBM_TOKEN env var); optional BYOK for `via: mothbackend`, which otherwise uses Moth's own credentials.
qpu_token.title: Qpu Token

ref_floor.description: |c_ref| below which F is null. Default: 4/sqrt(shots), ~0 for exact simulation.
ref_floor.title: Ref Floor

seed.description: RNG seed for the disorder realisation. Only audible when disorder > 0. Drawn as a 31-bit integer and returned in provenance if omitted. Capped at 2**53-1: above that, moth-api (Go) and any browser client re-spell the integer as a float64 and it stops matching the seed you sent.
seed.title: Seed

shots.description: Shots per circuit. Ignored when machine='aer' and exact=true. Above 8192 requires allow_high_shots.
shots.title: Shots

theta_x.description: Transverse kick per layer (RX angle, rad). The 'how quantum' dial: low → loud regular taps; high → inverted, attenuated, erased.
theta_x.title: Theta X

theta_z.description: Phase layer (RZ angle, rad). 0 → real, two-signed F. >0 → complex F: taps acquire a phase.
theta_z.title: Theta Z

theta_zz.description: Coupling per layer (RZZ, rad). Non-monotonic: ≈0.25π is the sparse setting. π is a Clifford (no scrambling). θ and π−θ coincide only when theta_x = 0, not at the default drive, so the upper half of the range is its own territory. The sign is invisible unless theta_z > 0.
theta_zz.title: Theta Zz

twirls.description: ZZ-commutant Pauli twirls per circuit, averaged. Randomises off-axis coherent rzz error (not angle miscalibration, which the reference run absorbs). Multiplies circuit count.
twirls.title: Twirls

via.description: How to reach the machine. `direct`: this engine drives qiskit-ibm-runtime itself (analytic emulation, native fractional gates, one batched QPU session). `mothbackend`: route through Moth's execution service, which holds the credentials — sampled only, so no analytic mode, no fractional gates, and one submission per circuit.
via.title: Via

otoc-echo-v1.description_md:
otoc-echo-v1 — Quantum Echo. A **core** engine.

Thin wrapper over the `quantum-echo` library: this file owns the platform contract
(params schema, validation, credits, estimate, the typed result envelope) and the
library owns the physics. Same relationship qdrive-api has with QDrive.

    params -> EchoSpec -> quantum_echo.measure_ir -> EchoIR.to_trajectory()

Media engines (retrocausal-echo-v1 and friends) depend on the same library and either
call `measure_ir` in-process or rebuild an IR from this engine's result with
`EchoIR.from_trajectory`. Neither path reimplements the measurement.

code_samples.source:
import time
import requests

API = "https://api.mothquantum.com"
# An explicit User-Agent is not optional: Cloudflare fronts this API and 403s
# the stdlib `Python-urllib/*` prefix with a plain-text `error code: 1010`
# body that looks exactly like an auth failure.
H = {"Authorization": "Bearer moth_YOUR_KEY",
     "User-Agent": "otoc-echo-example/1.0"}

def check(r):
    if not r.ok:                     # surface the body, or a 1010 is invisible
        raise RuntimeError(f"HTTP {r.status_code}: {r.text[:800]}")
    return r.json()

# 1. Submit. 202 and a job id -- params are validated in the worker's `build`
#    step, not here, so bad params come back as a job that fails.
job = check(requests.post(f"{API}/api/v1/engines/otoc-echo-v1/process", headers=H,
                          json={"params": {"n_sites": 8, "depth": 8,
                                           "theta_x": 0.9425, "theta_zz": 1.0996}}))["job_id"]

# 2. Poll.
while True:
    st = check(requests.get(f"{API}/api/v1/jobs/{job}/status", headers=H))
    if st["status"] in ("completed", "failed", "cancelled"):
        break
    time.sleep(1.5)
if st["status"] != "completed":
    raise RuntimeError(f"{st['status']}: {(st.get('error') or {}).get('message')} "
                       f"steps={{s['name']: s['status'] for s in st.get('steps', [])}}")

# 3. Read. The record sits at result.output; accept the looser shapes too.
body = check(requests.get(f"{API}/api/v1/jobs/{job}/result", headers=H))
env = body.get("result", body)
env = env.get("output", env)

print(env["result_type"])             # "trajectory"
print(env["extras"]["summary"])       # {live, inverted, regular, erased, complex, ...}
taps = env["extras"]["taps"]          # [{site, depth, F_re, F_im, level, polarity}, ...]

# Submit (202 + job_id), then poll /status, then read /result.
curl -X POST https://api.mothquantum.com/api/v1/engines/otoc-echo-v1/process \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer moth_YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "User-Agent: otoc-echo-example/1.0" \
  -d '{"params": {"lattice": "square", "width": 6, "height": 5, "depth": 6}}'

curl -s https://api.mothquantum.com/api/v1/jobs/$JOB_ID/result \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer moth_YOUR_KEY" -H "User-Agent: otoc-echo-example/1.0" \
  | jq '.result.output.extras.summary'

blur-v1.name: Quantum Blur
blur-v1.description: Apply a quantum blur algorithm to the image.

input_files.name: image
input_files.description: The image of your choice. The blur effect is applied RGB pixel values only, not the alpha channel. It means that if you submitted a PNG with transparent background, the background from the output will also be transparent.

input_files.name: mask
input_files.description:
Optional mask controlling where the effect is applied, on a per-pixel
basis. Must match the size of `image`. Each output pixel is a soft
blend `C = m · C_blurred + (1 - m) · C_original`, where `m` is the
normalised mask intensity at that pixel: black keeps the original,
white takes the fully blurred version, and grey values blend smoothly
between the two. Single-channel masks are used directly; RGB masks are
converted to luminance.

**Alpha-channel fallback**

If no mask is provided, the alpha channel of `image` is used instead
(transparent pixels keep the original, opaque pixels are blurred). For
RGB input with no alpha channel, the whole image is blurred.

downscale.description:
Strategy used when a mask region is larger than the maximum number of qubits allows:

- `true` — the region is downscaled to fit, blurred, and upscaled back.
- `false` — the region is split into adjacent tiles that are blurred independently.
downscale.title: Downscale

mask_bin_size.description: Mask quantisation step as a percentage of 255 (0–100). Pixel values below this threshold are treated as background, preventing near-zero JPEG/WebP compression artifacts from being detected as separate mask regions. Default 4 (~10/255).
mask_bin_size.title: Mask Bin Size

mask_min_region.description: Minimum mask region size in pixels. Connected components smaller than this are discarded after quantisation, removing residual compression artifacts that survive the binning step. Default 16.
mask_min_region.title: Mask Min Region

reach.description:
Controls how far from its original position a pixel can be affected by the blur:

- `0` — fully local: only nearby pixels are affected (default).
- `1` — fully non-local: pixels anywhere on the canvas can be affected equally.
reach.title: Reach

size.description: Pixel budget per blur pass: a region up to `size × size` pixels is blurred in a single pass. Internally converted to a qubit budget via `ceil(log2(size)) * 2`. Must be between 8 and 1024. Default 1024.
size.title: Size

strength.description:
Strength of the effect, which controls the rotation applied to each qubit:

- `0` — the image is left unchanged.
- `1` — maximum blur.
strength.title: Strength

style.description:
Quantum gate used to apply the effect:

- `rx` — rotation around the x-axis of the Bloch sphere.
- `ry` — rotation around the y-axis of the Bloch sphere.
style.title: Style

blur-v1.description_md:
Blur an image with a quantum rotation and get back an image of the same size and format, optionally only inside a masked region.

Each pixel's brightness is encoded into a quantum state, one rotation gate is
applied per qubit, and the state is read back into pixels. Because a single gate
moves weight across many pixels at once, the blur spreads as interference echoes
rather than a soft focus: shapes reappear faintly elsewhere on the canvas.
Colour images are processed one channel at a time; the alpha channel is untouched.

### How it works

1. Reads `image` and, if given, `mask`. Without a mask the alpha channel selects
   the region; RGB input with no alpha is blurred everywhere.
2. Splits the mask into connected regions and, for each, encodes the pixels into
   a statevector, applies the `style` rotation at the given `strength`, and reads
   the result back. Regions larger than `size` are downscaled or tiled per
   `downscale`.
3. Blends each blurred region with the original by mask intensity and writes the
   image in the input's format and dimensions.

### Output

One file in slot `result`: same format, dimensions and alpha channel as `image`.

### Limits

- Runs on a classical statevector simulator, not a QPU. Memory and time grow with
  region size; a 1024 x 1024 region uses 20 qubits.
- `strength` above 1 (with `reach` 0) starts to reverse the effect.
- `ry` on smooth gradients can collapse to a mostly dark image; prefer `rx` there.

### Further reading

- [QuantumBlur library](https://github.com/qiskit-community/QuantumBlur): the
  encoding and rotation this engine wraps.
- [ILA, Recurse](https://infinite.mothquantum.com): the album produced with this
  colour-channel technique.

telablur-v1.name: Quantum Teleblur
telablur-v1.description: Morph one image into another through quantum rotation gates.

input_files.name: image1
input_files.description: The source image. The teleblur effect morphs this image toward image2 through quantum rotation gates. Supported formats: PNG, JPEG, WebP, TIFF, BMP.

input_files.name: image2
input_files.description: The target image. The teleblur effect morphs image1 toward this image. If the dimensions differ from image1, image2 is resized to match before processing.

input_files.name: mask
input_files.description:
Optional mask controlling where the effect is applied, on a per-pixel
basis. Must match the size of `image1`. Each output pixel is a soft
blend `C = m · C_teleblurred + (1 - m) · C_image1`, where `m` is the
normalised mask intensity at that pixel: black keeps image1, white takes
the fully teleblurred result, and grey values blend smoothly between the
two. Single-channel masks are used directly; RGB masks are converted to
luminance.

**Alpha-channel fallback**

If no mask is provided, the alpha channel of `image1` is used instead
(transparent pixels keep image1, opaque pixels are teleblurred). For
RGB input with no alpha channel, the whole image is teleblurred.

direction.description:
Which qubits receive the blur rotation, controlling the spatial direction of the blur effect:

- `full` — all pixel qubits are rotated, producing blur in both directions (default).
- `vertical` — only the y-encoding qubits are rotated; the blur spreads vertically.
- `horizontal` — only the x-encoding qubits are rotated; the blur spreads horizontally.
direction.title: Direction

downscale.description: If True, oversized regions are downscaled before teleport and upscaled back. If False, oversized regions are tiled into adjacent sub-images.
downscale.title: Downscale

mask_bin_size.description: Mask quantisation step as a percentage of 255 (0–100). Pixel values below this threshold are treated as background, preventing near-zero JPEG/WebP compression artifacts from being detected as separate mask regions. Default 4 (~10/255).
mask_bin_size.title: Mask Bin Size

mask_min_region.description: Minimum mask region size in pixels. Connected components smaller than this are discarded after quantisation, removing residual compression artifacts that survive the binning step. Default 16.
mask_min_region.title: Mask Min Region

size.description: Pixel budget per teleblur pass: a region up to `size × size` pixels is teleported in a single pass. Must be between 8 and 1024. Default 1024.
size.title: Size

strength.description: Strength of the teleportation effect, between 0.0 and 1.0
strength.title: Strength

telablur-v1.description_md:
Quantum Teleblur — morphs one image into another through qubit rotations.

Both images are placed into a shared quantum state on n+1 qubits, where n
encodes the image pixels and one extra selector qubit identifies each image.
Rotating the selector qubit interpolates between the two images at the
amplitude level.

### Notes

- An optional `mask` selects where the effect is applied. If omitted,
  image1's alpha channel is used (RGBA) or the full image (RGB).
- The two images must share the same dimensions; mismatched sizes are
  rejected.
- Disjoint mask regions are processed independently from their bounding
  boxes.
- The simulator caps each region at `2 ** max_qubits` pixels. When a region
  exceeds that, `downscale=True` does downscale → teleport → upscale;
  `downscale=False` tiles the region. Output always matches input dimensions.
- The output is the composition (1-mask)·image1 + mask·teleblurred, where the
  teleblurred alpha is alpha1·(1-strength) + alpha2·strength.

retrocausal-echo-v1.name: Retrocausal Echo
retrocausal-echo-v1.description: A multi-tap delay whose tap map is measured on a quantum computer — negative returns invert, reverse or rotate the signal.

input_files.name: audio
input_files.description: Mono or stereo audio to process — WAV, MP3, OGG or FLAC. Stereo is summed to mono first, since the taps place their own stereo image. The file's own sample rate wins over the `sr` param.

input_files.name: ir
input_files.description: A previously measured impulse response — an otoc-echo `trajectory` envelope. Supply it to re-render without paying for the measurement again, and every echo param is ignored. Pass the asset id of a previous retrocausal-echo job's own `ir` output (output assets carry `slot` and `job_id`, so they chain straight into `input_files`), or upload the JSON yourself. `job:<id>/ir` is the documented alias for the same thing but may not resolve — prefer the asset id.

output_files.name: result
output_files.description: The primary output. With `emit: audio` (the default) this is the rendered stereo WAV. With `emit: map` no audio is rendered at all and this is the tap map as JSON — the same envelope the `taps` slot carries — so a sequencer or plugin can place the events itself without downloading audio.

output_files.name: ir
output_files.description: The impulse response actually used, as an otoc-echo `trajectory` envelope. Its output asset chains straight into another job's `input_files.ir` — one measurement, many mixes.

output_files.name: taps
output_files.description: The full `media` result envelope: provenance, the audio's shape, the echo summary, the spec, and the rendered tap map (time_ms, level, pan, F, polarity per tap). This is where a caller reads the numbers; a DAW or plugin can load it directly.

retrocausal-echo-v1.description_md:
retrocausal-echo-v1 — Retrocausal Echo. A **media** engine.

The other half of the split. `otoc-echo-v1` is the *core* engine: it measures a
quantum impulse response and returns it as a typed `trajectory`. This engine is a
*media* engine: it turns an impulse response into audio. Both depend on the same
`quantum-echo` library, so the measurement exists in exactly one place.

    core   : params -> EchoSpec -> measure_ir -> EchoIR.to_trajectory()
    media  : (EchoIR from a library call | a prior job's ir.json) -> MultiTapDelay -> WAV

Two ways in, one renderer:

  * no `ir` file  -> this engine calls `quantum_echo.measure_ir` in-process. One
    job, one price, audio out. The QPU work is identical to the core engine's.
  * an `ir` file  -> `EchoIR.from_trajectory`. Re-render a measured response with
    different audio, tempo, polarity behaviour or feedback without paying for the
    measurement again. The slot is `by_reference: true`, so it takes either an
    upload or `job:<id>/ir` off a previous retrocausal-echo job.

Nothing here builds a circuit and nothing in `render.py` knows what a qubit is.

code_samples.source:
import json
import os
import time
import requests

API = "https://api.mothquantum.com"
# Cloudflare 403s the stdlib `Python-urllib/*` User-Agent with a plain-text
# `error code: 1010`, which reads exactly like an auth failure. Always identify
# your client, and always print the response body on error.
H = {"Authorization": "Bearer moth_YOUR_KEY",
     "User-Agent": "retrocausal-echo-example/1.0"}

def check(r):
    if not r.ok:
        raise RuntimeError(f"HTTP {r.status_code}: {r.text[:800]}")
    return r.json()

def upload(path, content_type):
    """File inputs are assets, not multipart fields: create, PUT, complete.
    The presigned URL signs in the size and content type, so they must match."""
    size = os.path.getsize(path)
    a = check(requests.post(f"{API}/api/v1/assets", headers=H,
                            json={"filename": os.path.basename(path),
                                  "content_type": content_type, "size_bytes": size}))
    up = a["upload"]
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        r = requests.put(up["url"], data=fh, headers=up["headers"])
        if not r.ok:
            raise RuntimeError(f"upload HTTP {r.status_code}: {r.text[:400]}")
    check(requests.post(f"{API}/api/v1/assets/{a['asset_id']}/complete", headers=H))
    return a["asset_id"]

def run(params, input_files=None):
    job = check(requests.post(f"{API}/api/v1/engines/retrocausal-echo-v1/process", headers=H,
                              json={"params": params,
                                    "input_files": input_files or {}}))["job_id"]
    while True:
        st = check(requests.get(f"{API}/api/v1/jobs/{job}/status", headers=H))
        if st["status"] in ("completed", "failed", "cancelled"):
            break
        time.sleep(2)
    if st["status"] != "completed":
        raise RuntimeError(f"{st['status']}: {(st.get('error') or {}).get('message')}")
    return job, check(requests.get(f"{API}/api/v1/jobs/{job}/result", headers=H))

# 1. Measure and render in one job. No audio input -> you get the effect's own
#    stereo impulse response, ready for a convolver.
job, body = run({"n_sites": 10, "depth": 8, "theta_x": 1.2,
                 "negative_mode": "reverse", "ir_seconds": 4})

# Outputs come back as presigned URLs in `outputs`, on a separate S3 host.
# `result` is the WAV itself (the binary primary); `taps` carries the envelope.
out = {o["slot"]: o for o in (body.get("outputs") or [])}
open("retrocausal_ir.wav", "wb").write(requests.get(out["result"]["url"]).content)
taps = requests.get(out["taps"]["url"]).json()
print(taps["extras"]["tap_map"]["taps"][:3])

# 2. Re-render the same measured response over your own audio -- no quantum
#    work, 1 credit. The `ir` output asset chains straight into `input_files`.
job2, body2 = run(
    {"bpm": 128, "division": 0.75, "feedback": 0.55, "mix": 0.7},
    {"audio": upload("guitar.wav", "audio/wav"), "ir": out["ir"]["asset_id"]},
)
out2 = {o["slot"]: o for o in (body2.get("outputs") or [])}
open("guitar_retrocausal.wav", "wb").write(requests.get(out2["result"]["url"]).content)

# A WAV input is an asset, not a multipart field. Three calls to stage it:
#   POST /api/v1/assets  {filename, content_type, size_bytes}  -> presigned upload
#   PUT  <upload.url>    (with the exact headers it returns)
#   POST /api/v1/assets/{asset_id}/complete
# then pass the asset id in input_files:
curl -X POST https://api.mothquantum.com/api/v1/engines/retrocausal-echo-v1/process \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer moth_YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "User-Agent: retrocausal-echo-example/1.0" \
  -d '{"params": {"lattice":"square","width":5,"height":4,"depth":6,
                  "diffusion_ms":40,"negative_mode":"phase","theta_z":0.6,"mix":0.75},
       "input_files": {"audio": "<asset-uuid>"}}'

# Outputs are presigned URLs under `.outputs[]`, keyed by slot.
curl -s https://api.mothquantum.com/api/v1/jobs/$JOB_ID/result \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer moth_YOUR_KEY" -H "User-Agent: retrocausal-echo-example/1.0" \
  | jq '.outputs[] | {slot, url}'

error_codes.description: params fail Params' own field validation (type/range) or a cross-field check (square lattice without width/height, kick_site outside the line, shots over the cap without allow_high_shots).
the `ir` input is not UTF-8 JSON, or not an otoc-echo `trajectory` envelope. A bare envelope, a handler return wrapped in `output`, and a whole job result wrapped in `result` are all accepted.
the `audio` input could not be decoded as a PCM or float WAV, is over the size cap, or decoded to zero samples.
the input, or the input plus its computed tail, exceeds the render length cap. Set tail_ms explicitly or send a shorter file.
no tap survived min_level — the echo was fully erased at this theta_x, or min_level is too high. The echo summary is in the message.
the tap map is larger than the render cap. Raise min_level or lower depth.
the delay line needs more qubits than the machine allows — 24 for aer, the device's own width for an IBM backend. Supplying a measured `ir` sidesteps this entirely.
machine is neither 'aer' nor an IBM backend name the runtime knows.

the requested execution route could not be reached — for `via: direct`, qiskit-ibm-runtime is missing or no credentials were supplied (qpu_token param / QISKIT_IBM_TOKEN); for `via: mothbackend`, the mothbackend package is absent or the service returned a transport error. Retryable.
the estimator returned an error while running the echo circuits.
